The REST module reaches `VisitService.saveVisit` directly in three production places, all in the `openmrs1_9` resource classes that back `/ws/rest/v1`. Two test classes also call it.

**Direct production callers (best first):**
1. `VisitResource1_9.save` (line 251–254) is the `visit` resource's save hook. It returns `Context.getVisitService().saveVisit(visit)`, so every `POST`/`UPDATE` on `/visit` goes through it.
2. `VisitAttributeResource1_9.save` (line 96–116) calls `saveVisit(delegate.getVisit())` at line 114 after attaching or updating the attribute on its parent visit.
3. `VisitAttributeResource1_9.delete` (line 122–127) calls `saveVisit(delegate.getVisit())` at line 126 after voiding the attribute.

**Test callers, which would need updating if the behaviour changed:**
- `VisitController1_9Test` line 277.
- `EncounterController1_9Test` line 359.

**Indirect exposure, not verified:** core's `EncounterServiceImpl` calls `saveVisit` at line 257 when saving an encounter. Any REST encounter resource that saves through `EncounterService` would therefore see the change too. I did not open the REST encounter resource to confirm its call path. `PatientResource1_9` and `VisitConfigurationController2_0` only read visits, so they are not affected by a save-behaviour change.
